task.title: Compare long numeric prerelease identifiers without int conversion (python-semver issue #487)
task.statement: python-semver (src/semver, BSD-3) is a semantic-versioning library whose central class is semver.version.Version (also exported as semver.Version). Bug report (upstream issue #487): Version.is_valid("0.0.0-" + "1" * 5000) is True, but Version.parse("0.0.0-" + "1" * 5000).compare(...) raises ValueError, because Version._nat_cmp in src/semver/version.py converts every all-digit prerelease identifier with int() and CPython refuses int conversion of strings longer than 4300 digits. Fix the prerelease comparison in src/semver/version.py so that it never converts a long ASCII numeric identifier to an int, while keeping the existing ordering rules exactly. Required semantics of the prerelease comparison: identifiers are the dot-separated parts of the prerelease string (an empty or None prerelease has one empty identifier); an identifier consisting only of ASCII digits is numeric and compares by its decimal value, computed without int(): strip leading zeros (an all-zero identifier becomes "0"), compare by length first and then lexicographically; a numeric identifier is lower than any non-numeric identifier; two non-numeric identifiers compare as plain strings; when every identifier of the shorter list is equal, the longer list is higher. Preserve the constructor's legacy behaviour: Version(0, 0, 0, prerelease=...) accepts identifiers with leading zeros and identifiers written with non-ASCII decimal digits (str.isdigit() is true), and such non-ASCII digit identifiers keep comparing by their int() value, so "١٢" compares equal to "12" and "１２" is lower than "13"; an identifier for which str.isdigit() is true but int() fails (for example "²") must still make compare() raise ValueError, eagerly, even when an earlier identifier would already decide the order, but only when the core versions are equal: a difference in major, minor or patch is decided before the prerelease is examined, so Version(0, 0, 0, prerelease="²") < Version(1, 0, 0, prerelease="²") is True. Keep everything else unchanged: Version.parse keeps rejecting non-canonical prereleases such as "01", "01.2", "١٢" and "１２" with ValueError; build metadata is ignored in comparisons; a version with a prerelease is lower than the same core version without one; the prerelease attribute is stored as given. Do not change parsing, the optional native parser, tests, docs or packaging files, and keep the whole existing pytest suite passing.
acceptance_criteria: With v = "0.0.0-" + "1" * 5000: Version.is_valid(v) is True; Version.parse(v).compare(v) == 0; compare(v, "0.0.0-2") == 1 and compare("0.0.0-2", v) == -1 (no ValueError).

Ordering of long numeric prereleases with Version.parse("0.0.0-" + x): "9" * 4999 < "1" + "0" * 4999; "1" + "0" * 4998 + "1" < "1" + "0" * 4998 + "2"; "1" * 5000 < "alpha"; "alpha." + "1" * 5000 < "alpha." + "1" * 5000 + ".1". For each pair low.compare(high) == -1, high.compare(low) == 1 and sorted([high, low]) == [low, high].
Build metadata is ignored and release order is preserved: with version = Version.parse("0.0.0-" + "1" * 5000), version == version.replace(build="other") and version < Version(0, 0, 0).

Constructor prereleases compare with the legacy rules, as Version(0, 0, 0, prerelease=left).compare(Version(0, 0, 0, prerelease=right)): ("0001", "1") -> 0; ("000", "0") -> 0; ("02", "10") -> -1; ("01.2", "1.2") -> 0; ("2a", "10a") -> 1; ("01a", "1a") -> -1; ("-1", "0") -> 1; ("", None) -> 0; ("١٢", "12") -> 0; ("１２", "13") -> -1; ("1٢", "12") -> 0; ("٠٠١", "1") -> 0; the reverse comparison gives the negated result and both .prerelease attributes are stored as given.
Version.parse("0.0.0-" + p) raises ValueError for p in ("01", "01.2", "١٢", "１２").
Version(0, 0, 0, prerelease=left).compare(Version(0, 0, 0, prerelease=right)) raises ValueError for (left, right) in (("²", "2"), ("a.²", "b.0"), ("a.0", "b.²")).
Version(0, 0, 0, prerelease="²") < Version(1, 0, 0, prerelease="²") is True (the core comparison decides before the prerelease is examined).
The existing pytest suite in tests/ passes unchanged.

spec.restated_task: Update prerelease comparison in src/semver/version.py so ASCII numeric identifiers of arbitrary length compare by normalized decimal strings without integer conversion. Preserve existing version precedence, constructor permissiveness, Unicode digit conversion behavior and eager conversion errors, parsing restrictions, stored attributes, public interfaces, and the unchanged test suite.

interface_contract.name: Version
interface_contract.signature: Version(major: SupportsInt, minor: SupportsInt = 0, patch: SupportsInt = 0, prerelease: Optional[Union[String, int]] = None, build: Optional[Union[String, int]] = None)
interface_contract.behavior: Available as semver.Version and semver.version.Version; VersionInfo remains its alias. Constructor behavior is unchanged: core components are converted to integers; prerelease and build are stored as None or str(argument). String prereleases retain their exact contents, including leading zeros, empty strings, and Unicode digits. Construction does not validate prerelease identifiers.
error_cases: ValueError: a converted core component is negative.
TypeError or ValueError: existing core integer conversion fails.

interface_contract.name: Version._nat_cmp
interface_contract.signature: @classmethod def _nat_cmp(cls, a: Optional[str], b: Optional[str]) -> int
interface_contract.behavior: This existing internal comparison boundary returns exactly -1, 0, or 1. Split each input on dots, treating None and an empty string as one empty identifier and retaining empty identifiers inside lists. A nonempty ASCII digit-only identifier is numeric: remove leading zeros, representing all-zero values as '0', and compare numeric values by normalized length followed by lexicographic order, without int conversion. An identifier containing non-ASCII characters for which str.isdigit() is true retains legacy int(identifier) conversion and numeric classification; its value compares numerically with ASCII and other Unicode numeric identifiers. Every remaining identifier is non-numeric. Numeric identifiers precede non-numeric identifiers; two non-numeric identifiers use Python string ordering. Compare corresponding identifiers in order, then list lengths if all paired identifiers are equal. Preserve eager conversion of digit-only non-ASCII identifiers throughout both inputs before returning any ordering result.
error_cases: ValueError: int(identifier) fails for any digit-only non-ASCII identifier anywhere in either input, including an unpaired suffix or an identifier following an already decisive pair. Preserve interpreter conversion-limit failures for this legacy Unicode path.
ASCII numeric identifier length must never cause an integer-conversion ValueError.

interface_contract.name: Version.compare
interface_contract.behavior: Preserve supported operands: Version instances compatible with the existing class check, strings, bytes, dictionaries, tuples, and lists. Preserve operand parsing/construction. Return exactly -1, 0, or 1. Compare major, minor, and patch first; if they differ, return without examining prerelease identifiers. For equal cores, perform the eager prerelease comparison described above. None and empty prereleases are equivalent absence of prerelease; a nonempty prerelease precedes absence. Ignore build metadata. Do not mutate either operand.
error_cases: TypeError: unsupported operand type, under existing rules.
TypeError or ValueError: existing operand parsing or construction fails.
ValueError: equal-core prerelease comparison encounters a digit-only non-ASCII identifier whose int conversion fails, even when prerelease presence or an earlier identifier could decide ordering.

interface_contract.name: Version comparison operators
interface_contract.signature: def __eq__(self, other: Comparable) -> bool; def __ne__(self, other: Comparable) -> bool; def __lt__(self, other: Comparable) -> bool; def __le__(self, other: Comparable) -> bool; def __gt__(self, other: Comparable) -> bool; def __ge__(self, other: Comparable) -> bool
interface_contract.behavior: Continue deriving supported-operand results from compare(), including sorting and build-insensitive equality. Preserve the existing decorator's NotImplemented behavior for unsupported operands and collections that cannot construct a version.
error_cases: ValueError: propagated from prerelease comparison for otherwise supported operands.
Preserve existing Python operator behavior after NotImplemented, including TypeError for unsupported ordering.

interface_contract.name: Version.parse
interface_contract.signature: @classmethod def parse(cls: Type[T], version: String, optional_minor_and_patch: bool = False) -> T
interface_contract.behavior: Unchanged. Parse canonical SemVer strings or UTF-8 bytes, preserving subclass construction and optional minor/patch behavior. Long canonical ASCII numeric prereleases remain accepted. Leading-zero numeric prereleases and non-ASCII prerelease digits remain rejected.
error_cases: ValueError: invalid SemVer input, including prereleases '01', '01.2', '١٢', and '１２'.
UnicodeDecodeError: invalid UTF-8 byte input, as before.

interface_contract.name: Version.is_valid
interface_contract.behavior: Unchanged. Return True when parse succeeds and False when parse raises ValueError, including True for the specified 5000-digit canonical prerelease.
error_cases: Exceptions not caught by the existing ValueError handler continue to propagate.

interface_contract.name: semver.compare
interface_contract.signature: def compare(ver1: str, ver2: str) -> int
interface_contract.behavior: Keep the existing deprecated wrapper, warning behavior, and delegation to Version.parse(ver1).compare(ver2). Long ASCII numeric prereleases receive the corrected ordering.
error_cases: Propagate existing parsing and comparison errors.

interface_contract.name: Version.replace
interface_contract.behavior: Unchanged. Return a new version with specified parts replaced. Replacing only build metadata must preserve comparison equality, including for long numeric prereleases.
error_cases: TypeError: unknown replacement keys, as before.
Preserve existing constructor errors for replacement values.

acceptance_criteria: 1. For v = '0.0.0-' + '1' * 5000, Version.is_valid(v) is True, Version.parse(v).compare(v) is 0, semver.compare(v, '0.0.0-2') is 1, and the reverse comparison is -1, without ValueError.

2. For parsed equal-core versions, each pair is strictly ascending: ('9' * 4999, '1' + '0' * 4999), ('1' + '0' * 4998 + '1', '1' + '0' * 4998 + '2'), ('1' * 5000, 'alpha'), and ('alpha.' + '1' * 5000, 'alpha.' + '1' * 5000 + '.1'). For every pair, low.compare(high) == -1, high.compare(low) == 1, and sorted([high, low]) == [low, high].
3. For version = Version.parse('0.0.0-' + '1' * 5000), version == version.replace(build='other') and version < Version(0, 0, 0). Comparison leaves all stored attributes unchanged.

4. Using Version(0, 0, 0, prerelease=p), the following (left, right, result) cases hold: ('0001', '1', 0), ('000', '0', 0), ('02', '10', -1), ('01.2', '1.2', 0), ('2a', '10a', 1), ('01a', '1a', -1), ('-1', '0', 1), ('', None, 0), ('١٢', '12', 0), ('１２', '13', -1), ('1٢', '12', 0), and ('٠٠١', '1', 0). Reverse comparisons negate the result, and both prerelease attributes retain exactly their supplied strings or None.

5. Constructor prereleases with long leading-zero ASCII identifiers use normalized values: '0' * 5000 equals '0', '0' * 5000 + '1' equals '1', and '0' * 5000 + '2' is lower than '10'. A 5000-digit nonzero ASCII identifier also compares numerically above the Unicode identifier '١٢', without converting the ASCII identifier to int.

6. Identifier splitting preserves empty parts. Direct _nat_cmp('', None) == 0, _nat_cmp('a', 'a.') == -1, _nat_cmp('a..b', 'a..c') == -1, and _nat_cmp('', '0') == 1. At the version level, empty and None prereleases are equivalent releases and both rank above any nonempty valid prerelease.

7. Version.parse('0.0.0-' + p) raises ValueError for each p in ('01', '01.2', '١٢', '１２'); Version.is_valid returns False for those same version strings. Parsing rules and native-parser integration remain unchanged.

8. Equal-core constructor comparisons raise ValueError for ('²', '2'), ('a.²', 'b.0'), and ('a.0', 'b.²'), and for their reversals. Eagerness also applies to unpaired suffixes, such as ('a', 'a.²'), and release comparisons, such as ('²', None). No specific new exception message is required.

9. Core precedence bypasses prerelease examination: Version(0, 0, 0, prerelease='²') < Version(1, 0, 0, prerelease='²') is True. Equivalent cases differing first in minor or patch also return the core ordering without ValueError; reverse comparisons negate it.

10. ASCII numeric comparison uses no int conversion, including after removing leading zeros, and does not raise, disable, or otherwise modify the interpreter's integer-string conversion limit. On CPython with that facility, run the 5000-digit cases with the limit enabled at 4300 and confirm the setting is unchanged afterward.
11. All existing tests in tests/ pass unchanged, including operand coercion, invalid-operand behavior, subclass behavior, parsing, and optional-backend tests.
12. The implementation diff is confined to src/semver/version.py and the prerelease comparison fix; existing public signatures and unrelated behavior are unchanged.

limitations: Profile 'eval-attest-a1': inference provider codex_gateway; submission runs must use NVIDIA Nemotron on Nebius Token Factory and are labeled separately.

Sealed and adversarial suites run one child process per test under a supervisor that never imports candidate code and is the first step of its branch; two verifier canaries detect blanket result forgery. A candidate can still forge its own result from inside a child after the nonce was read if it spares the canaries (the mutation gate and held-out tests are the structural detectors).

The repository's own suite and the held-out suite run after the sealed verification in their own branches. They are bound through the same supervisor only for unittest repositories whose tests are statically discoverable; otherwise they are parsed from console output and the gate is labelled evidence_class 'stdout'.

Model-written sealed and adversarial tests can be wrong; their failures block VERIFIED. An independent arbiter classifies each failure (implementation bug, test defect or contract dispute) and, for pure test defects, offers a corrected module. The correction counts only after mechanical validation (same test methods, only the failing ones changed, passes on the candidate, still fails on the unmodified base or is caught by a mutant); the corrected gate is then re-run and the verdict re-derived from the gates. A sealed test that failed by assertion is never overridden. The classification itself remains a model judgement.

INFEASIBLE is recorded only when a witness program written by the contract auditor demonstrated the contradiction by running on the unmodified repository (exit code and output recorded); the witness's logic is the model's, its execution is not.
Grounding runs only when the specification names external references; sources are cited, not verified for correctness.
Sandbox CPU/RAM quota controls were not found in the current public REST API; per operation only max_layer_bytes, a timeout and the networking flag are set.
Sandbox raw 'cost' diagnostics are not USD; Codex gateway usage is ChatGPT allowance, not a Nebius charge; Nebius USD is computed from the public price table, not an invoice.
Each run retains one checkpoint image on the service; no image-delete control was found in the current public REST API.

manifest.json lists the sha256 of every artifact and `python -m attest check <run dir or zip>` recomputes digests, the sealed and adversarial bindings from verify_raw.json and the gate-to-verdict rule offline; it cannot re-execute the sandbox runs themselves.
